commands.name: deep-research
commands.description: Deep research harness — fan-out web searches, fetch sources, adversarially verify claims, synthesize a cited report. (dynamic workflow)

commands.name: design
commands.description: Grant or revoke Claude agent access to your Design projects

commands.name: design-sync
commands.description: Push a React design system to claude.ai/design. This runs a converter that bundles the real component code (from Storybook or a bare package) and uploads it. Use when the user runs /design-sync or says "sync my design system to Claude Design".

commands.name: dataviz
commands.description: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. When the destination is a first-party document connector (host-designated, never self-described) that renders live charts, hand it the rows (inline, or as an uploaded data file the chart cites) rather than a rendered PNG/SVG — a picture of a chart loses hover, data inspection and per-value comments. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".

commands.name: update-config
commands.description: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.

commands.name: verify
commands.description: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes; bootstraps this repo's project verify skill if none exists yet. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.

commands.name: debug
commands.description: Enable debug logging for this session and help diagnose issues

commands.name: code-review
commands.description: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs (plus reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups where the model's review recipe covers them) at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.

commands.name: simplify
commands.description: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.

commands.name: batch
commands.description: Research and plan a large-scale change, then execute it in parallel across 5–30 isolated worktree agents that each open a PR.

commands.name: fewer-permission-prompts
commands.description: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.

commands.name: doctor
commands.description: Health-check the user's Claude Code setup and fix issues: diagnose installation health — what the `claude doctor` terminal diagnostics cover — from local data (duplicate or leftover installs, PATH, unparseable settings files, broken or colliding agent definitions, skills whose frontmatter fails to parse); find unused skills, MCP servers, and plugins versus their context cost and disable dead weight; deduplicate local CLAUDE.md files against checked-in ones; trim checked-in CLAUDE.md files by cutting content a session could derive from the codebase (directory layouts, tech-stack lists, architecture overviews) while keeping gotchas, rationale, and non-standard conventions; migrate always-loaded CLAUDE.md guidance into lazy skills and nested CLAUDE.md files; flag slow hooks and context-heavy extensions; check the installed version is current; make auto mode the default permission mode; and pre-approve frequently denied read-only commands. Use when the user asks for a doctor run, checkup, audit, tune-up, or cleanup of their Claude Code setup or configuration.

commands.name: loop
commands.description: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace.

commands.name: claude-api
commands.description:
Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).

commands.name: workflow-authoring
commands.description: Reference for writing a Workflow tool script (script API and gotchas, resume, quality patterns, worked examples). Load before authoring a script for a workflow the user already opted into; it does not itself authorize running one.

commands.name: run
commands.description: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

commands.name: run-skill-generator
commands.description: Author or improve the run-<unit> skill - a per-project skill that tells agents how to build, launch, and drive this project's app. Use when the user asks to set up the project, get it running, write run instructions, or verify build/run steps work from a clean environment.

commands.name: advisor
commands.description: Let Claude consult a stronger model at key moments

commands.name: agents
commands.description: (removed) Ask Claude to create/manage subagents, or edit .claude/agents/

1	# ActionLedger: guide for agents
2	
3	This page is the whole interface. An agent that reads it should be able to use ActionLedger without reading
4	the source code.
5	
6	## What it offers
7	
8	ActionLedger is an HTTP service you call **instead of** calling a side-effecting tool directly. You send it a
9	write, it records the request durably, performs the write once, and tells you what happened. When the tool's
10	reply is lost (a timeout, a dropped acknowledgement), ActionLedger checks the tool's real state before
11	answering, so you do not have to guess whether to retry.
12	
13	The tool behind this deployment is a task tracker that is **not idempotent**: two creates make two tasks.
14	ActionLedger currently supports one tool, `tracker.create_task`.
15	
16	## Access
17	
18	- Base URL: given to you by the operator, for example `http://127.0.0.1:8000`.
19	- Authentication: send the header `X-Agent-Key: <key>` on every call except `/health`. The operator gives you
20	  the key.
21	- All bodies are JSON (`Content-Type: application/json`).
22	- A machine-readable schema is at `GET /openapi.json`.
23	- Use a client timeout of at least 15 seconds. A call normally returns in milliseconds, but it can take a few
24	  seconds when ActionLedger has to verify an uncertain write.
25	
26	## Operations
27	
28	| Call | Purpose |
29	|---|---|
30	| `POST /execute` | Perform one write, or repeat a request you already sent |
31	| `GET /status/{action_id}` | Read the recorded outcome of one action; re-verifies it if it was uncertain |
32	| `GET /actions?workflow_id=...` | List the outcomes of every action in a workflow, oldest first |
33	| `GET /health` | Liveness check, no key needed; returns `{"ok": true}` |
34	
35	### `POST /execute`: inputs
36	
37	| Field | Type | Required | Meaning |
38	|---|---|---|---|
39	| `action_id` | string, 1–180 chars | yes | Your name for this one logical write. **You choose it.** The same `action_id` always means the same write |
40	| `workflow_id` | string, 1–120 chars | yes | Groups the actions of one job so they can be listed later |
41	| `tool` | string | no | Must be `tracker.create_task` (the default) |
42	| `payload` | JSON object | yes | The task to create, stored as given |
43	
44	Payload fields for `tracker.create_task`:
45	
46	| Field | Type | Meaning |
47	|---|---|---|
48	| `title` | string | The task title |
49	| `parent_resource_id` | string, optional | The `resource_id` of the task this one depends on, for example `"task_1"` |
50	
51	Other payload fields are stored unchanged.
52	
53	### Outputs
54	
55	`POST /execute` and `GET /status/{action_id}` return HTTP 200 with:
56	
57	| Field | Meaning |
58	|---|---|
59	| `action_id` | The id you sent |
60	| `status` | The outcome, see the next table |
61	| `resource_id` | The id of the created task, for example `"task_1"`; `null` if no task is known to exist |
62	| `safe_to_retry` | `true` only when `status` is `SAFE_TO_RETRY` |
63	| `evidence` | What ActionLedger saw: the tracker's reply, or the lookup result, or a `reason` |
64	
65	`GET /actions?workflow_id=...` returns `{"actions": [ ... ]}`, one such object per action. An unknown
66	workflow returns an empty list.
67	
68	### What each status means and what to do
69	
70	| `status` | Meaning | What you should do |
71	|---|---|---|
72	| `CONFIRMED_SUCCESS` | The tracker acknowledged the write | Continue. Use `resource_id` |
73	| `RECOVERED_SUCCESS` | The reply was lost, but ActionLedger found exactly one task with this action's tag and the same payload | Continue. Use `resource_id` exactly as for a confirmed write. Do not create the task again |
74	| `SAFE_TO_RETRY` | The write is known not to have happened | Send the identical request again, with the same `action_id` |
75	| `FAILED` | The tracker rejected the request before doing anything | Do not repeat it unchanged. Fix the request or report the failure |
76	| `AMBIGUOUS` | ActionLedger cannot tell whether the write happened (lookup is unavailable, or the result is not a single clean match) | **Stop this step. Do not send the write again under a new `action_id`**; that can create a duplicate. Report it. You may call `GET /status/{action_id}` later; it re-checks and can turn into `RECOVERED_SUCCESS` |
77	| `PENDING`, `EXECUTING`, `UNKNOWN` | The action is still in progress or has not been verified yet | Wait a few seconds and call `GET /status/{action_id}` |
78	
79	### Choosing `action_id`
80	
81	- Derive it from the job and the step, for example `inc-204:step-2`, so that the same step always gets the
82	  same id, including after you restart.
83	- Repeating a request with the same `action_id` and the same body is always safe: you get the recorded
84	  outcome and no second write.
85	- A new `action_id` is a new write. Never invent a fresh id to "try again".
86	
87	### Resuming work
88	
89	If you take over a workflow, or you restarted and lost your memory, call
90	`GET /actions?workflow_id=<id>` first. It shows which actions already exist and their `resource_id`s. Reuse
91	those results; do not recreate them.
92	
93	## Errors
94	
95	Errors return a JSON body `{"detail": ...}`.
96	
97	| HTTP | `detail` | Meaning |
98	|---|---|---|
99	| 401 | `Invalid agent key` | Missing or wrong `X-Agent-Key` |
100	| 403 | `Tool not allowlisted` | `tool` is not `tracker.create_task` |
101	| 404 | `Unknown action` | `GET /status` for an `action_id` that was never sent |
102	| 409 | `action_id already bound to a different request` | You reused an `action_id` with a different `workflow_id`, `tool` or `payload` |
103	| 422 | a list of field errors | The body or query is missing a field or has the wrong type |
104	
105	## Permissions and limits
106	
107	- One agent key, one tool (`tracker.create_task`). ActionLedger cannot read, update, close or delete tasks.
108	- It only vouches for writes that went through it. Calling the tracker directly bypasses all protection.
109	- `AMBIGUOUS` is a real answer, not an error: this is not a universal exactly-once guarantee.
110	- One ledger process, local use only. No rate limit is enforced; calls are handled one at a time.
111	
112	## Setup (operator)
113	
114	Python 3.11+.
115	
116	```bash
117	git clone https://github.com/Cecilia1220/actionledger.git
118	cd actionledger
119	python3 -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate
120	pip install -r requirements.txt
121	cp .env.example .env            # sets AGENT_KEY=local-demo-agent for local use
122	python -m uvicorn mock_tracker:app --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8001 --workers 1 &
123	python -m uvicorn ledger:app --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8000 --workers 1 &
124	curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8000/health
125	```
126	
127	## One small example
128	
129	```bash
130	curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/execute \
131	  -H 'X-Agent-Key: local-demo-agent' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
132	  -d '{"action_id":"trip42:step1","workflow_id":"trip42","tool":"tracker.create_task","payload":{"title":"Investigate"}}'
133	```
134	
135	```json
136	{"action_id": "trip42:step1", "status": "CONFIRMED_SUCCESS", "safe_to_retry": false,
137	 "resource_id": "task_1",
138	 "evidence": {"resource_id": "task_1", "tag": "trip42:step1", "payload_hash": "02e0809e…"}}
139	```
140	
141	A dependent task then uses that id:
142	
143	```bash
144	curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/execute \
145	  -H 'X-Agent-Key: local-demo-agent' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
146	  -d '{"action_id":"trip42:step2","workflow_id":"trip42","tool":"tracker.create_task","payload":{"title":"Plan","parent_resource_id":"task_1"}}'
147	```

# ActionLedger: guide for agents

This page is the whole interface. An agent that reads it should be able to use ActionLedger without reading
the source code.

## What it offers

ActionLedger is an HTTP service you call **instead of** calling a side-effecting tool directly. You send it a
write, it records the request durably, performs the write once, and tells you what happened. When the tool's
reply is lost (a timeout, a dropped acknowledgement), ActionLedger checks the tool's real state before
answering, so you do not have to guess whether to retry.

The tool behind this deployment is a task tracker that is **not idempotent**: two creates make two tasks.
ActionLedger currently supports one tool, `tracker.create_task`.

## Access

- Base URL: given to you by the operator, for example `http://127.0.0.1:8000`.
- Authentication: send the header `X-Agent-Key: <key>` on every call except `/health`. The operator gives you
  the key.
- All bodies are JSON (`Content-Type: application/json`).
- A machine-readable schema is at `GET /openapi.json`.
- Use a client timeout of at least 15 seconds. A call normally returns in milliseconds, but it can take a few
  seconds when ActionLedger has to verify an uncertain write.

## Operations

| Call | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `POST /execute` | Perform one write, or repeat a request you already sent |
| `GET /status/{action_id}` | Read the recorded outcome of one action; re-verifies it if it was uncertain |
| `GET /actions?workflow_id=...` | List the outcomes of every action in a workflow, oldest first |
| `GET /health` | Liveness check, no key needed; returns `{"ok": true}` |

### `POST /execute`: inputs

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `action_id` | string, 1–180 chars | yes | Your name for this one logical write. **You choose it.** The same `action_id` always means the same write |
| `workflow_id` | string, 1–120 chars | yes | Groups the actions of one job so they can be listed later |
| `tool` | string | no | Must be `tracker.create_task` (the default) |
| `payload` | JSON object | yes | The task to create, stored as given |

Payload fields for `tracker.create_task`:

| Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `title` | string | The task title |
| `parent_resource_id` | string, optional | The `resource_id` of the task this one depends on, for example `"task_1"` |

Other payload fields are stored unchanged.

### Outputs

`POST /execute` and `GET /status/{action_id}` return HTTP 200 with:

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `action_id` | The id you sent |
| `status` | The outcome, see the next table |
| `resource_id` | The id of the created task, for example `"task_1"`; `null` if no task is known to exist |
| `safe_to_retry` | `true` only when `status` is `SAFE_TO_RETRY` |
| `evidence` | What ActionLedger saw: the tracker's reply, or the lookup result, or a `reason` |

`GET /actions?workflow_id=...` returns `{"actions": [ ... ]}`, one such object per action. An unknown
workflow returns an empty list.

### What each status means and what to do

| `status` | Meaning | What you should do |
|---|---|---|
| `CONFIRMED_SUCCESS` | The tracker acknowledged the write | Continue. Use `resource_id` |
| `RECOVERED_SUCCESS` | The reply was lost, but ActionLedger found exactly one task with this action's tag and the same payload | Continue. Use `resource_id` exactly as for a confirmed write. Do not create the task again |
| `SAFE_TO_RETRY` | The write is known not to have happened | Send the identical request again, with the same `action_id` |
| `FAILED` | The tracker rejected the request before doing anything | Do not repeat it unchanged. Fix the request or report the failure |
| `AMBIGUOUS` | ActionLedger cannot tell whether the write happened (lookup is unavailable, or the result is not a single clean match) | **Stop this step. Do not send the write again under a new `action_id`**; that can create a duplicate. Report it. You may call `GET /status/{action_id}` later; it re-checks and can turn into `RECOVERED_SUCCESS` |
| `PENDING`, `EXECUTING`, `UNKNOWN` | The action is still in progress or has not been verified yet | Wait a few seconds and call `GET /status/{action_id}` |

### Choosing `action_id`

- Derive it from the job and the step, for example `inc-204:step-2`, so that the same step always gets the
  same id, including after you restart.
- Repeating a request with the same `action_id` and the same body is always safe: you get the recorded
  outcome and no second write.
- A new `action_id` is a new write. Never invent a fresh id to "try again".

### Resuming work

If you take over a workflow, or you restarted and lost your memory, call
`GET /actions?workflow_id=<id>` first. It shows which actions already exist and their `resource_id`s. Reuse
those results; do not recreate them.

## Errors

Errors return a JSON body `{"detail": ...}`.

| HTTP | `detail` | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| 401 | `Invalid agent key` | Missing or wrong `X-Agent-Key` |
| 403 | `Tool not allowlisted` | `tool` is not `tracker.create_task` |
| 404 | `Unknown action` | `GET /status` for an `action_id` that was never sent |
| 409 | `action_id already bound to a different request` | You reused an `action_id` with a different `workflow_id`, `tool` or `payload` |
| 422 | a list of field errors | The body or query is missing a field or has the wrong type |

## Permissions and limits

- One agent key, one tool (`tracker.create_task`). ActionLedger cannot read, update, close or delete tasks.
- It only vouches for writes that went through it. Calling the tracker directly bypasses all protection.
- `AMBIGUOUS` is a real answer, not an error: this is not a universal exactly-once guarantee.
- One ledger process, local use only. No rate limit is enforced; calls are handled one at a time.

## Setup (operator)

Python 3.11+.

```bash
git clone https://github.com/Cecilia1220/actionledger.git
cd actionledger
python3 -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate
pip install -r requirements.txt
cp .env.example .env            # sets AGENT_KEY=local-demo-agent for local use
python -m uvicorn mock_tracker:app --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8001 --workers 1 &
python -m uvicorn ledger:app --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8000 --workers 1 &
curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8000/health
```

## One small example

```bash
curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/execute \
  -H 'X-Agent-Key: local-demo-agent' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"action_id":"trip42:step1","workflow_id":"trip42","tool":"tracker.create_task","payload":{"title":"Investigate"}}'
```

```json
{"action_id": "trip42:step1", "status": "CONFIRMED_SUCCESS", "safe_to_retry": false,
 "resource_id": "task_1",
 "evidence": {"resource_id": "task_1", "tag": "trip42:step1", "payload_hash": "02e0809e…"}}
```

A dependent task then uses that id:

```bash
curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/execute \
  -H 'X-Agent-Key: local-demo-agent' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"action_id":"trip42:step2","workflow_id":"trip42","tool":"tracker.create_task","payload":{"title":"Plan","parent_resource_id":"task_1"}}'
```
